metadata.ethicsOpinions: EMPLOYEE DID NOT ΓÇ£PARTICIPATEΓÇ¥ IN THE MATTER. The requestor is a former Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) employee who now works at a private company that is interested in submitting a bid on a TxDOT project. While employed by TxDOT, the requestor was involved with review of the schematic of a particular construction project. The requestor left TxDOT before the completion of the schematic and the development of the design plans. The proposal will be released for public bids in September 2025, more than three years after the requestor left TxDOT. The request- orΓÇÖs current employer is planning on submitting a bid for the construction management contract and would like to list the requestor on the proposal. If awarded the contract, the requestor anticipates his ΓÇ£role during construction management would be constructability review. The requestorΓÇÖs limited work on the schematic is too attenuated from the contract for the construction management of the project to say that he ΓÇ£participatedΓÇ¥ in the construction management contract as a state employee. Therefore, he may receive compensation for services rendered on behalf of his private employer for the construction management contract. EAO 627. See also, EAO 507 (2012), EAO 477 (2007), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 337 (1996). ΓÇ£PARTICULAR MATTERΓÇ¥ AS IT PERTAINS TO A COMMISSIONER. A TCEQ Commissioner requested an opinion asking at what point a particular permit- ting or enforcement action comes within the ΓÇ£official responsibilityΓÇ¥ of a commissioner for purposes of the law. Section 572.054(b) does not apply to all enforcement or permitting matters for which an investigation was conducted or an application/registration was received before the commissioner left office. Instead, the provision applies only to matters that were submitted to the com- missioners for consideration before the commissioner left office. EAO 621 (2025). NO REVOLVING DOOR PROHIBITION WHEN WORKING ON PROJECTS NOT WORKED ON AT AGENCY. The requestor is a former employee of the Texas General Land Office (GLO) who worked as a project manager overseeing regional planning studies funded through Community Block Development Grants (CDBG) provided by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The projects the requester oversaw were large regional flood studies and interagency agreements with other state agencies. The GLO has a separate planning grant program called the Resilient Communities Program (RCP). RCP awards planning grants to cities and counties for local planning activities. The requestor was not involved in the RCP program while at the GLO. The requestor now operates his own business that provides grant services to cities and counties. The Section 572.045(b) revolving door restriction does not apply to the requestor because the requestor will be providing services to only cities and counties. EAO 613. See also, EAO 573 (2002). STATE EMPLOYEE MAY NOT BE EMPLOYED IF HE PARTICIPATED IN CONTRACTS. Requestor is an employee of HHSC who plans on leaving to join a company with several state contracts. He expects to help manage payments to the state each month as well as helping with eligibility and quality control, but will not engage with the state contracts with HHSC. These are different particular matters than his work with the HHSC, so neither 572.054 would apply. This is the first opinion to address a state contract negotiation that was not also a procurement, but the same principle applies ΓÇô if the requestor gave approval, advice or recommendation on whether to enter into a contract at all, he participated and would be prohibited from employment with the company for 2 years. EAO 600. See also, Revolving Door #2: EAO 496 (2011), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997). Revolving Door #3: EAO 568 (2021), EAO 545 (2017). INTERTWINING 	SBOE, 	TEA, 	PERMANENT SCHOOL 	FUND 	CORP 	REVOLVING 	DOOR QUESTION. The requestor is a former member of the State Board of Education ΓÇô all revolving door provisions will apply. Under 572.054(a): he must wait two years before appearing before or seeking to influence both the Commissioner of Education (officer of SBOE) and the PSF Corporation (because the Corporation board con- tains SBOE members). He would also be restricted with respect to TEA employees if they were also employees of the SBOE under the common law employee/er test. Under 572.054(b): since he participated in contracts that SBOE sent to PSF Corporation, he may not ever receive compensation under contracts that he participated in as an SBOE member. Under 572.069: he may not accept employment for two years from any person involved in any transactions which were subject to a ratification vote by the SBOE board during his tenure there. EAO 598. See also, Revolving Door #1: EAO 545 (2017), EAO 381 (1997). Revolving Door #2: EAO 496 (2011), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997). Revolving Door #3: EAO 586 (2023), EAO 571 (2022), EAO 568 (2021) STATE AGENCY IS NOT A ΓÇ£PERSONΓÇ¥ FOR REVOLVING DOOR PURPOSES. The requestor is a state employee who is considering whether to accept a position in the private sector. In his current position, he has no working relationship with the potential employer. He does not review any contractual deliverables submit- ted by the potential employer to his state agency, nor does he exercise any judgment regarding the potential employerΓÇÖs performance or payment. The requestor previously held a different position with the same state agency; however, in that capacity he ΓÇ£had no individual nor management responsibility for procurement ofΓÇ¥ the services provided by the potential employer. Nor was he involved in the selection or over- sight of the potential employer. Section 572.054(b) does not prohibit former state employees from accepting a position with any employer; it merely prohibits them from working on certain ΓÇ£particular matters.ΓÇ¥ Tex. GovΓÇÖt Code ┬º 572.054(b). As long as the position does not require him to work on any particular matter in which he participated as a public servant, Section 572.054(b) does not prohibit him from accepting the position. EAO 579 (2022). STATE AGENCY IS NOT A ΓÇ£PERSONΓÇ¥ FOR REVOLVING DOOR PURPOSES. All three revolv- ing door provisions prohibit former state officers and employees from representing, accepting employment, or receiving compensation from certain ΓÇ£person[s].ΓÇ¥ As defined by Chapter 572, a state agency is not a ΓÇ£person,ΓÇ¥ so none of the revolving door provisions restrict former state officers and employees from accepting employment with another state agency. EAO 573 (2022). SEPARATE RFPΓÇÖS ARE SEPARATE ΓÇ£MATTERSΓÇ¥. Like separate contracts, separate RFPs leading to sepa- rate contracts are separate ΓÇ£mattersΓÇ¥ for purposes of the revolving door provision in Government Code section 572.054(b). However, the conclusion that a specific work activity constitutes ΓÇ£participation inΓÇ¥ one matter does not necessarily preclude the conclusion that the same work also constitutes ΓÇ£participation inΓÇ¥ another matter. [W] e caution agency officers and employees against using their authority to cancel a procurement for essential state services with an intent to profit from their knowledge of the agencyΓÇÖs inevitable search for a new provider. EAO 570 (2022). See also EAO 397 (1998). FORMER 	TCEQ 	EMPLOYEE 	WORKING 	AS CONTRACTOR WITH PRIVATE FIRM. A for- mer TCEQ employee responsible for reviewing reports related to reimbursement of expenses for contractors did not prohibit the former employee from working as a con- tractor subsequently to work with the agency, with some limitations based on previous work. EAO 539. See also EAO 523 (2014), EAO 507 (2012), EAO 496 (2011), EAO 419 (1999), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997), EAO 353 (1996), EAO 345 (1996), EAO 337 (1996), EAO 324 (1996). TXDOT EMPLOYEE SUBSEQUENT WORK ON PROJECT HE WAS INVOLVED IN AT AGENCY. A former TXDOT employee is not prohibited from subsequently providing services on different parts of a large-scale project than those which he oversaw as an employee. EAO 523. See also EAO 507, EAO 496, EAO 397, EAO 364, EAO 353, EAO 345, EAO 324, EAO 285. TXDOT 	EMPLOYEE 	WORK 	ON 	HIGHWAY CONSTRUCTION PROJECT. A former TXDOT employee may perform services on behalf of a private employer regarding a general engineering consultant contract to oversee a design-build contract if the ser- vices do not include a review or analysis of any highway design and construction provisions that are essential components of the design-build contract in which he was involved. EAO 507. See also EAO 397, EAO 364, EAO 337. GENERAL WORK ON SAME SUBJECT MATTER NOT PROHIBITED. The fact that two matters relate to the same general subject matter of a proposed agency project does not make them part of the same particu- lar matter. The revolving door provision also does not prohibit former state employees from working in subject areas or for employers with which they became familiar in the course of their state employment. EAO 496. See also EAO 419, EAO 353, EAO 345, EAO 324, EAO 364. MEMBER OF TEXAS BOARD OF PROFESSIO- NAL LAND SURVEYING SHOULD NOT SERVE AS EXPERT WITNESS ON MATTER UNDER JURISDICTION OF BOARD. A member of the Texas Board of Professional Land Surveying should not serve as an expert witness to testify on whether a person had committed a violation of laws, rules, or standards within the jurisdiction of the board. EAO 492. See also EAO 410, EAO 318. FORMER 	EMPLOYEE 	OF 	AGENCY 	NOT PROHIBITED FROM WORKING ON BID FOR CONTRACT WITH THAT AGENCY. A former employee of a regulatory agency would not violate Government Code section 572.054(b) by working on a private companyΓÇÖs bid for an agency contract that utilizes the standard specifications as described in this request that the requestor participated in writing as an agency employee. EAO 477. See also EAO 365. AGENCY 	ATTORNEY 	WORKING 	ON 	CASE AFTER LEAVING. The revolving door provision in section 572.054(b) of the Government Code does not prohibit a former assistant general counsel for a state agency from representing a person in a case that was opened while the former assistant general counsel was an employee for the agency if as a state employee she did not personally participate in the case and if the case was not within her official responsibility. EAO 470. See also EAO 285. FORMER EMPLOYEE OF STATE AGENCY WHO TESTIFIED AS EXPERT ON AGENCY RULES AT 	TRIAL 	DURING 	EMPLOYMENT 	MAY SUBSEQUENTLY REPRESENT ONE OF THE PARTIES IN THAT LAWSUIT. An individual for- merly employed by a state regulatory agency who, while an employee for the state agency testified as an expert on the state agencyΓÇÖs rules in a lawsuit to which the state of Texas was not a party, may represent a litigant in that lawsuit. EAO 469. CONTRACT ENTERED INTO FOR 3 YEARS, WITH OPTION TO EXTEND TO 4 YEARS, IS CONSIDERED ΓÇ£PARTICULAR MATTERΓÇ¥ FOR THE ENTIRE 4 YEARS. This opinion considers the meaning of the term ΓÇ£particular matterΓÇ¥ for purposes of the revolving door provision in Government Code sec- tion 572.054(b) in a situation in which a state agency and a private entity entered into a contract for services that provided for a three-year term and gave the agency the option to extend the contract for a fourth year. In our opinion, the entire four-year period is part of the same matter for purposes of the revolving door provision in Government Code section 572.054(b). EAO 446. See also EAO 397. THOUGH TWO AGENCIES WORK TOGETHER ON A PROJECT, ONE AGENCYΓÇÖS DECISIONS ON THE PROJECT CONSTITUTE A SEPARATE MATTER FROM THE OTHER AGENCY. Even though two agencies may work together on a particular project, one agencyΓÇÖs decisions in regard to the project constitute a separate matter from the other agencyΓÇÖs decisions in regard to the project. Therefore, the former employee of the Department of Health may work on the matter of the contract decision to be made by the Health and Human Services Commission. Any level of partici- pation in a matter triggers the revolving door prohibition in section 572.054(b). EAO 438. See also EAO 292, EAO 285, EAO 275. FORMER EMPLOYEE HELPING TO WRITE BOOK ABOUT SUBJECT MATTER RELATING TO WORK WITH AGENCY. All tasks that are part of a regulatory agencyΓÇÖs involvement in negotiating or executing a book endorsement contract are part of the ΓÇ£matterΓÇ¥ of the book endorsement. If a former employee of the state agency participated in any of those tasks, then the former employee could not receive compensation from a publisher for writing any part of the material that would be the subject of the contemplated endorsement. EAO 426. See also EAO 365, EAO 345, EAO 246, EAO 232, EAO 220. FORMER REGULATORY AGENCY EMPLOYEE ACCEPTING WORK ON PROJECT FUNDED BY AGENCY. A former employee of a regulatory agency would not violate Government Code section 572.054(b) by working on a project funded by that agency which is similar to other project applications that the employee worked on while at the agency. EAO 419. See also EAO 365, EAO 364, EAO 353, EAO 345, EAO 246, EAO 232, EAO 324, EAO 337, and EAO 397. SEPARATE 	CONTRACTS 	ARE 	SEPARATE ΓÇ£MATTERSΓÇ¥ 	FOR 	PURPOSES 	OF 	THE REVOLVING DOOR PROVISION. The conclusion that a specific work activity constitutes ΓÇ£participation inΓÇ¥ one matter, however, does not necessarily preclude the conclusion that the same work also constitutes ΓÇ£partici- pation inΓÇ¥ another matter. EAO 397. See also EAO 364, EAO 337. TXDOT FORMER EMPLOYEE WHO PARTICI- PATED IN ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY. A for- mer employee of the Department of Transportation who participated in the matter of the acquisition of a specific piece of property may not represent a private business entity or receive compensation from a private business entity for services in regard to the departmentΓÇÖs acquisi- tion of the same piece of property. The matter of assuring compliance with an agency rule or policy is not part of the same matter as the matter of drafting or adopting the agency rule or policy. EAO 365. See also EAO 353, EAO 345, EAO 246, EAO 232, EAO 337, EAO 52. FORMER EMPLOYEE OF LOTTERY COMMIS- SION. As long as a former Lottery Commission employeeΓÇÖs new job does not involve a specific contract he worked on or any other specific matter he worked on as a Lottery Commission employee, his work for a private employer he previously dealt with as a Lottery Commission employee will not bring him into violation of the revolving door provision in Government Code sec- tion 572.054(b). EAO 364. See also EAO 353, EAO 345, EAO 255, EAO 275. STATE AGENCY NOT REQUIRED TO PROVIDE FORMER 	EMPLOYEE 	WITH 	A 	LIST 	OF ΓÇ£MATTERSΓÇ¥ THAT THEY WORKED ON WHILE EMPLOYED THERE. Chapter 572 of the Government Code does not place an obligation on a state agency to provide a former employee with a list of matters in which the former employee participated. A former employee is, of course, entitled to request information under the Open Records Act. Id. ch. 552. Previous attorney general opinions have stated, however, that the Open Records Act does not require an agency to prepare new information or to prepare answers to questions. Open Records Decision Nos. 617 (1993); 555 (1990). EAO 361. See also Open Records Decision 617, 555. PROHIBIT 	FORMER 	AGENCY 	EMPLOYEE PURCHASING DECISIONS. A former employee who had been involved, as an agency employee, in a decision about specific purchasing needs of the agency could not leave the agency and receive compensation for assisting a vendor in attempting to sell something to the agency to satisfy those specific needs. Section 572.054(b) does not, however, prohibit a former agency employee who worked on some specific purchasing decisions for an agency from performing work for a vendor in connection with other purchasing decisions by the agency. EAO 353. FORMER AGENCY EMPLOYEE WHO WORKED ON 	FEDERAL 	GRANT 	APPLICATION 	FOR AGENCY. The fact that a former state employee worked on an agency grant application seeking federal funds does not prohibit the former state employee from work- ing on a response to the agencyΓÇÖs request for proposals for projects to be funded by grant proceeds, nor from working on the project itself. EAO 345. See also EAO 232, EAO 246, EAO 324, EAO 337. PREVIOUS 	EMPLOYEE 	OF 	COMPTROLLER MAY 	NOT 	PROVIDE 	LEGAL 	ADVICE 	TO TAXPAYER RE: TAX AUDIT. The lawyer, as an employee of the Comptroller, provided advice in connec- tion with the audit. A sales tax audit and a redetermina- tion proceeding in which the audit findings are disputed are part of the same ΓÇ£matterΓÇ¥ for purposes of section 572.054(b) of the Government Code. EAO 337. See also EAO 23. REVOLVING DOOR DOES NOT APPLY TO FORMER EMPLOYEE FOR ALL ASPECTS OF PROJECT, BUT RATHER ONLY THE PART ON WHICH THEY WORKED. The revolving door pro- vision in Government Code section 572.054(b) does not prohibit a former employee of the Texas Natural Resource Conservation Commission from working on the certification of a groundwater monitoring system even though the former employee reviewed and approved or supervised the review and approval of the ground- water monitoring system during the permit application process while employed by the agency. The certification of a groundwater monitoring system and the review of a permit application are separate matters. EAO 324. See also EAO 23, EAO 233. FORMER COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCIES. The revolving door statute does not restrict a former commissioner or deputy commissioner of the Texas Health and Human Services Commission from engaging in activities on behalf of per- sons seeking action from one of the health and human services agencies within the purview of the commission. EAO 292. See also EAO 232, 246; ┬º531.021, Government Code. COMPENSATION 	IN 	CONNECTION 	WITH MATTER OVER WHICH FORMER EMPLOYEE HAD AUTHORITY. The revolving door law restricts certain former state officers and employees from receiv- ing compensation in connection with any matter over which the former officer or employee had authority, even if the former officer or employee was not aware that his subordinates were working on the matter. See Green v. State, 773 S.W.2d 816 (Tex. App.ΓÇöSan Antonio 1989, no pet.) (Penal statutes are not construed so strictly as to defeat the obvious legislative intent). EAO 285. FORMER MEMBER OF TEXAS COMMISSION ON FIRE PROTECTION. The revolving door provi- sions in section 572.054 of the Government Code do not prohibit a former member of the Texas Commission on Fire Protection from serving on an advisory committee to the commission. EAO 278. See also EAO 232. FORMER OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE TEXAS NATURAL RESOURCE CONSEVATION COMMISSION. Generally, former members of the governing boards of state agencies and former executive directors of state agencies are subject to the two revolving door provisions in section 572.054 of the Government Code. Former officers and employees of the TNRCC should look to Health and Safety Code sections 361.0885 and 382.0591 and Water Code section 26.0283, not to section 572.054 of the Government Code, to determine whether they may work on a permit matter. EAO 275. See also EAO 233. FORMER 	EMPLOYEE 	OF 	TEXAS 	REAL ESTATE COMMISSION TEACHING COURSES TO PREPARE APPLICANTS FOR LICENSING EXAMINATION. The revolving door provision in sec- tion 572.054(b) of the Government Code does not pre- vent a former employee of the Real Estate Commission who was involved in the administration of real estate examinations from teaching courses to prepare appli- cants to take the real estate licensing examination. EAO 255. See also EAO 232. FORMER 	EMPLOYEE 	OF 	A 	REGULATORY AGENCY 	TEACHING 	COURSES 	REQUIRED FOR 	RECERTIFICATION 	OF 	PESTICIDE APPLICATORS. A former employee of a regulatory agency may teach courses required for recertification of pesticide applicators provided that he did not work on the applications for recertification of any of his students. EAO 251. See also EAO 232. FORMER GENERAL COUNSEL OF THE TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF INSURANCE. A former general counsel of the Texas Department of Insurance is not sub- ject to the revolving door provisions in section 572.054 of the Government Code. EAO 250. See also EAO 233. FORMER MEMBER OF THE STATE BOARD OF EDUCATION. The revolving door provisions of section 572.054 of the Government Code do not prohibit a for- mer member of the State Board of Education from rep- resenting a textbook publisher in a matter to be decided by a local school board. EAO 246. See also EAO 232, EAO 154. FORMER 	TEXAS 	NATURAL 	RESOURCE CONSERVATION COMMISSION EMPLOYEES. Former employees of the Texas Natural Resources Conservation Commission are subject to the revolving door provisions in section 572.054 of the Government Code with the following exception: A former TNRCC employee who participated in the handling of a permit application covered by Health and Safety Code sections 361.0885 and 382.0591 or Water Code section 26.0283 is subject to those provisions, not to section 572.054 of the Government Code, for purposes of determining whether he or she may represent a person in regard to a permit matter before the TNRCC. We note that the attorney general issued an opinion determining that Government Code section 572.054 does not apply to employees of the Public Utilities Commission (PUC), because the Public Utilities Regulatory Act (PURA) prohibits former employees from post-employment work on matters in which they were involved as employees. Unlike the statutes under consideration in this opinion, the PURA restrictions apply to all PUC employees, and so the Government Code prohibition is inapplicable to all PUC employees. EAO 233. See also, Attorney General Opinion DM-209 (1993) Affirmed by EAO 275 (1995) FORMER EMPLOYEE OF A STATE AGENCY COMMUNICATING TO THE LEGISATURE. The revolving door provisions of the Government Code do not prohibit a former officer or employee of a regulatory agency from working for a nonprofit entity or govern- mental body after ceasing employment with the agency. Nor does it prohibit a former officer or employee of a regulatory agency from performing work for a law firm on behalf of a nonprofit entity or governmental body. Government Code section 572.054 does not prohibit a former employee of a state agency from communicat- ing to the legislature in regard to statutes affecting the agency because pending legislation is not a ΓÇ£particular matterΓÇ¥ for purposes of section 572.054(b). In contrast, we think that an agencyΓÇÖs decision about agency rec- ommendations to the legislature would be a ΓÇ£particular matterΓÇ¥ for purposes of the revolving door provisions. EAO 232. See also, EAO 220, EAO 229. FORMER STATE EMPLOYEE AS INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. A state agency is not a person for purposes of chapter 572. Therefore, the revolving door prohibition in section 572.054(b) of the Government Code does not prohibit a former agency employee from working for the agency as an independent contractor. EAO 229. See also, EAO 220, 214, 44. IF AN ORGANIZATION IS NOT CONSIDERED A 	PERSON 	UNDER 	CHAPTER 	572, 	THE REVOLVING 	DOOR 	PROHIBITION 	IS 	NOT APPLICABLE. A former board memberΓÇÖs activities on behalf of a non-profit organization is not restricted because the organization is neither an individual nor a ΓÇ£business entity,ΓÇ¥ and thus it is not a ΓÇ£personΓÇ¥ for pur- poses of chapter 572 and the revolving door prohibition. Thus section 572.054(a) is not applicable to the former board memberΓÇÖs actions on behalf of this organization. EAO 220. See also, EAO 213; Attorney General Opinion JM-671 (1987), Attorney General Letter Opinion 93-12 (1993). PAST 	EMPLOYEE 	SERVING 	IN 	PUBLIC RELATIONS FOR A STATE AGENCY. An individ- ual formerly employed by a state regulatory agency to perform public relations work for the purpose of achiev- ing public support for proposed legislation may perform public relations work for the same purpose for a private foundation without violating Government Code section 572.054(b). EAO 212. LEGISLATOR 	MAY 	ENGAGE 	IN 	NEGOTIA- TIONS 	FOR 	FUTURE 	EMPLOYMENT 	BUT MAY NOT NEGOTIATE LEGISLATIVE ACTION DURING TERM. Nothing in the laws subject to interpretation by the Ethics Commission specifically addresses the issue of a legislator engaging in negotia- tions for future employment. The bribery law would prohibit a legislator from accepting or soliciting future employment in exchange for some official action on the part of the legislator during the remainder of his term of office. There may be laws outside of the commissionΓÇÖs jurisdiction that would be applicable. For example, The Texas Constitution contains a ΓÇ£contracts clause,ΓÇ¥ which bars legislators from entering into any contract with the state or county when such contract has been authorized or funded by a legislature of which the individual was a member. Tex. Const. art. III, ┬º 18; see also id. art. III, ┬º 22 (requiring disclosure and recusal by legislator who has an interest in a pending bill); GovΓÇÖt Code ┬º 572.053 (member of the legislature prohibited on voting on a measure benefitting certain business transactions in which legislator has an interest). EAO 205. See also, EAO 41, EAO 28. FORMER 	HEARING 	SUPERVISOR 	MAY REPRESENT PARTIES IN ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS BEFORE AGENCY EXCEPT FOR MATTERS 	WORKED 	ON 	WHILE 	AT 	THE AGENCY. A former state agency employee subject to section 572.054(b) may represent a person before his for- mer agency so long as he does not work on a matter in which he participated or for which he had responsibility as a state employee. Further, a former employee may work on matters that are similar to matters he worked on as a state employee, and he may work for a person or entity that he dealt with as a state employee, as long as he does not work on a matter he worked on as a state employee or a matter over which he had responsibility as a state employee. EAO 197. See also EAO 23, EAO 154. MEMBERS OF TCSGA BOARD. The Texas Certified Self-Insurer Guaranty Association (TCSGA) board of directors is not a state agency for purposes of chapter 572, and the revolving door prohibition is inapplicable to the self-insurer members of the TCSGA board. EAO 179. See also EAO 142. STATE AGENCY MAY REFUSE TO DEAL WITH FORMER 	EMPLOYEE 	ATTEMPTING 	TO REPRESENT AN INDIVIDUAL IN VIOLATION OF 572.054(b). A former state officer or employee of a regulatory agency covered by Government Code section 572.054(b) commits an offense if the former officer or employee represents any person or receives any com- pensation for services rendered on behalf of any person regarding a particular matter in which the former offi- cer or employee participated during the period of state service or employment, either through personal involve- ment or because the case or proceeding was a matter within the officerΓÇÖs or employeeΓÇÖs official responsibility. An agency may refuse to deal with a former officer or employee who attempts to represent an individual in violation of the statute, consistent with the due process rights of the individuals concerned. Nothing in the statutes the Texas Ethics Commission is authorized to interpret directly provides that a state officer or employee commits an offense by permitting a prohibited represen- tation to take place, or that a person commits an offense by allowing himself to be represented in violation of the statute, though section 7.02 of the Penal Code provides for criminal responsibility for the conduct of another under certain circumstances. EAO 167. TEXAS COMMISSION ON THE ARTS. The com- mission was created by statute. It also has rulemaking authority. Therefore the Commission on the Arts is a regulatory agency for purposes of section 7A of article 6252-9b, V.T.C.S. EAO 154. TEXAS BOARD OF PARDONS AND PAROLES. The Board of Pardons and Paroles is a regulatory agency for purposes of section 7A of article 6252-9b, V.T.C.S. EAO 79. TEXAS 	LOW-LEVEL 	RADIOACTIVE 	WASTE DISPOSAL 	AUTHORITY. 	The 	Texas 	Low-level Radioactive Waste Disposal Authority is a ΓÇ£regulatory agencyΓÇ¥ for purposes of article 6252-9b, section 7A. The fact that the interests of a private employer coincide with the interests of a state agency does not relieve a former employee of the state agency from the burdens of section 7A. EAO 52. FORMER 	BOARD 	MEMBERS 	PROHIBITED FROM 	APPEARING 	ON 	BEHALF 	OF 	ANY PERSON, INCLUDING ONESELF. For two years after the date a former board member of the governing body of a regulatory agency ceases to be a member of the agency, that person is prohibited from making an appearance before or communicating with current offi- cers and agency employees, with the intent to influence, on behalf of any person in connection with any matter on which the person seeks official action. The prohibi- tion applies to appearances or communications that the former official makes on his own behalf, except as limited by the due process clause of the United States Constitution. The prohibition applies regardless of whether the former official initiates the contact with his former agency or whether the action sought is ever taken. EAO 44. See also EAO 11. UNSALARIED 	BOARD 	MEMBER 	OF 	STATE AGENCY NOT PROHIBITED FROM MAKING POLITICAL CONTRIBUTIONS. Chapter 302 does include a limitation on direct expenditures for corre- spondence that is applicable to any individual, including appointed officers, [t]herefore, an unsalaried state officer may make contributions to candidates for public office or to candidates for the Office of Speaker of the House of Representatives but may not expend more than $100 for the cost of correspondence to aid or defeat the election of a speaker candidate. EAO 24. ΓÇ£DIVISION 	HEADΓÇ¥ 	NOT 	CONSIDERED ΓÇ£EXECUTIVE HEADΓÇ¥ FOR APPLICATION OF REVOLVING DOOR. Article 6252-9b does not define ΓÇ£executive head.ΓÇ¥ That term, however, is generally understood to refer to the highest ranking employee of a board. Consequently, we conclude that it would not include employees below that rank such as the division head described in the requestorΓÇÖs letter. If a former employee advised his current employer in regard to an audit in which he had participated during his tenure with the state agency, he would be receiving compen- sation for services rendered in regard to that matter. Therefore, a former employee may not provide such advice. EAO 23. REVOLVING DOOR PROVISION ONLY APPLIES TO FORMER MEMBER OF GOVERNING BODY WHO CEASES SERVICE ON OR AFTER 1/1/1992. Subsection (a) of section 7A of article 6252-9b applies only to a person who ceases service with the state on or after January 1, 1992. EAO 11.

sections.title: CERTAIN SOLICITATIONS OF REGULATED BUSINESS ENTITIES
sections.content: PROHIBITED; CRIMINAL OFFENSE (a) 	An association or organization of employees of a regulatory agency may not solicit, accept, or agree to accept anything of value from a business entity regulated by that agency and from which the business entity must obtain a permit to operate that business in this state or from an individual directly or indirectly connected with that business entity. (b) 	A business entity regulated by a regulatory agency and from which the business entity must obtain a permit to operate that business in this state or an individual directly or indirectly connected with that business entity may not offer, confer, or agree to confer on an association or organization of employees of that agency anything of value. (c) 	This section does not apply to an agency regulating the operation or inspection of motor vehicles or an agency charged with enforcing the parks and wildlife laws of this state. (d) 	A person commits an offense if the person intentionally or knowingly violates this section. An offense under this subsection is a Class A misdemeanor.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 1993, 73 rd Leg., ch. 268, Sec. 1, eff. Sept. 1, 1993.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: EMPLOYEE 	ORGANIZATION 	OF 	REGULA- TORY 	AGENCY 	EMPLOYEES 	DONATIONS. Section 572.055 of the Government Code restricts an organization made up of employees of a regulatory agency from seeking or obtaining donations from a busi- ness entity that must obtain a permit from the regulatory agency. Further, it restricts an organization made up of employees of a regulatory agency from seeking or obtain- ing donations from an individual directly or indirectly connected to a business entity that must obtain a permit from the regulatory agency. The restriction in section 572.055 that applies to an individual ΓÇ£directly or indi- rectly connected toΓÇ¥ a business entity applies to owners and employees of a business entity and to creditors whose right to payment depends on the profits of the business. The restriction does not apply to customers of a business entity. EAO 213.

sections.title: CONTRACTS BY STATE OFFICERS WITH GOVERNMENTAL
sections.content: ENTITIES; CRIMINAL OFFENSE (a) 	A state officer may not solicit or accept from a governmental entity a commission, fee, bonus, retainer, or rebate that is compensation for the officerΓÇÖs personal solicitation for the award of a contract for services or sale of goods to a governmental entity. (b) 	This section does not apply to: (1) 	a contract that is awarded by competitive bid as provided by law and that is not otherwise prohib- ited by law; or (2) 	a court appointment. (c) 	In this section, ΓÇ£governmental entityΓÇ¥ means the state, a political subdivision of the state, or a govern- mental entity created under the Texas Constitution or a statute of this state. (d) 	A state officer who violates this section commits an offense. An offense under this subsection is a Class A misdemeanor.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 1993, 73 rd Leg., ch. 268, Sec. 1, eff. Sept. 1, 1993.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: LEGISLATOR PAYMENT FROM LAW FIRM FOR SERVICES RENDERED IN A CAPACITY OTHER THAN AS PUBLIC SERVANT. A legislator may accept payment from a law firm for services rendered to the law firm as long as the services were rendered in a capacity other than as a public servant. In any case, Ethics Advisory Opinion No. 72 (1992) stated that sec- tion 572.056 which prohibits legislators from accepting payments from governmental bodies is so vague as to be unenforceable. EAO 283. See also EAO 72.

sections.title: CERTAIN LEASES PROHIBITED
sections.content: (a) 	Except as provided by Subsection (d), a member of the legislature, an executive or judicial officer elected in a statewide election, or a business entity in which the legislator or officer has a substantial interest may not lease any office space or other real property to the state, a state agency, the legislature or a legislative agency, the Supreme Court of Texas, the Court of Criminal Appeals, or a state judicial agency. (b) 	A lease made in violation of Subsection (a) is void. (c) 	This section does not apply to an individual who is an elected officer on June 16, 1989, for as long as the officer holds that office. (d) 	A member of the legislature or a business entity in which the legislator has a substantial interest may donate the use of office space that the member or entity owns and that is located in the memberΓÇÖs district to the house of the legislature in which the member serves to be used for the memberΓÇÖs official business. Office space donated under this subsection is not a contribution for purposes of Title 15, Election Code. Acceptance of a donation of office space under this subsection is not subject to Section 301.032.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 1993, 73 rd Leg., ch. 268, Sec. 1, eff. Sept. 1, 1993. Amended by Acts 2013, 83rd Leg., R.S., Ch. 293 (H.B. 1256), Sec. 1, eff. September 1, 2013.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: INTERVENTION IN PRIVATE REAL ESTATE TRANSACTIONS. Questions about the legal effect of private real estate transactions are outside the scope of the Ethics CommissionΓÇÖs authority. EAO 440.

sections.title: PRIVATE INTEREST IN MEASURE OR DECISION; DISCLOSURE;
sections.content: REMOVAL FROM OFFICE FOR VIOLATION (a) 	An elected or appointed officer, other than an officer subject to impeachment under Article XV, Section 2, of the Texas Constitution, who is a member of a board or commission having policy direc- tion over a state agency and who has a personal or private interest in a measure, proposal, or decision pending before the board or commission shall publicly disclose the fact to the board or commission in a meeting called and held in compliance with Chapter 551. The officer may not vote or otherwise participate in the decision. The disclosure shall be entered in the minutes of the meeting. (b) 	An individual who violates this section is subject to removal from office on the petition of the attorney general on the attorney generalΓÇÖs own initiative or on the relation of a resident or of any other member of the board or commission. The suit must be brought in a district court of Travis County or of the county where the violation is alleged to have been committed. (c) 	If the court or jury finds from a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant violated this section and that an ordinary prudent person would have known the individualΓÇÖs conduct to be a violation of this section, the court shall enter judgment removing the defendant from office. (d) 	A suit under this section must be brought before the second anniversary of the date the violation is alleged to have been committed, or the suit is barred. (e) 	The remedy provided by this section is cumulative of other methods of removal from office provided by the Texas Constitution or a statute of this state. (f) 	In this section, ΓÇ£personal or private interestΓÇ¥ has the same meaning as is given to it under Article III, Section 22, of the Texas Constitution, governing the conduct of members of the legislature. For purposes of this section, an individual does not have a ΓÇ£personal or private interestΓÇ¥ in a measure, pro- posal, or decision if the individual is engaged in a profession, trade, or occupation and the individualΓÇÖs interest is the same as all others similarly engaged in the profession, trade, or occupation.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 1993, 73 rd Leg., ch. 268, Sec. 1, eff. Sept. 1, 1993.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: MEMBER 	OF 	NON 	PROFIT 	HOSPITAL ADVISORY BOARD MUST RECUSE HIMSELF. A member of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board who is also a nonvoting member of the advisory board of a nonprofit entity should disclose his position with the nonprofit entity and recuse himself from any Coordinating Board decision regarding acceptance of a donation of land from the nonprofit entity or regarding approval of an agreement between the nonprofit entity and a state university. EAO 412. TREC MEMBERS CANNOT TEACH COURSES TO SATISFY TREC REQUIREMENTS WITHOUT VIOLATING STANDARDS OF CONDUCT. State officers should comply with the standards of conduct set out in section 572.051 Government Code, by not engag- ing in conduct proscribed by those standards of conduct. When conflicts of interest nonetheless arise, state offi- cers must recuse themselves in accordance with section 572.058. Recusal would not cure a violation of the stan- dards of conduct set out in section 572.051. A member of the Texas Real Estate Commission (ΓÇ£TRECΓÇ¥) should not teach courses that satisfy TREC requirements for prospective or current licensees. EAO 410. See also EAO 318, EAO 311. MEMBER OF BOARD OF TDHCA WHO HAS SUBMITTED BID OR AWARDED CONTRACT UNDER DEPARTMENTΓÇÖS PROGRAMS MUST DISCLOSE AND RECUSE. A member of the board of the Department of Housing and Community Affairs who owns a construction company and bids on a project of a developer applying for tax credits under a tax credit program administered by the department must recuse himself from matters involving the developer. If this sit- uation arises, the member should therefore disclose the fact that he has an interest in the matter in a meeting called under the Open Meetings Act, and recuse him- self not only from voting, but from any participation in the matter. EAO 298. See also EAO 218, EAO 256, Attorney General Opinion H-1319 (1978), Attorney General Opinion JM-671 (1987). See generally ┬º572.058, Government Code. OFFERING CONTINUING EDUCATION COUR- SES FOR PROFIT. There is an exception to the prohi- bition for fees for services, but the exception is applicable only if the fee is for services rendered in a capacity other than as a public servant. A member of the Board of Vocational Nurse Examiners should not offer continuing education courses for profit for vocational nurses seeking license renewal. EAO 257. See also EAO 192; 22 TAC 237.15-237.17. BOARD MEMBER OF STATE AGENCY MUST DISCLOSE INTEREST AND RECUSE HIMSELF. In a situation in which a member of the governing board of a state agency has a personal or private interest in a matter pending before the board, section 572.058 of the Government Code requires that the board member dis- close the interest and recuse himself from participation in the matter. Section 572.058 does not require the board member to divest himself of the interest. EAO 256. See also EAO 218. IF AN ORGANIZATION IS NOT CONSIDERED A 	PERSON 	UNDER 	CHAPTER 	572, 	THE REVOLVING 	DOOR 	PROHIBITION 	IS 	NOT APPLICABLE. A former board memberΓÇÖs activities on behalf of a non-profit organization is not restricted because the organization is neither an individual nor a ΓÇ£business entity,ΓÇ¥ and thus it is not a ΓÇ£personΓÇ¥ for purposes of chapter 572 and the revolving door prohibition. Thus section 572.054(a) is not applicable to the former board memberΓÇÖs actions on behalf of this organization. In par- ticular, we note that Attorney General Opinion JM-671 (1987) held that section 6 of former article 6252-9b, now Government Code section 572.058(a), did not change the common law conflict of interest rule prohibiting contracts between a governmental body and an entity in which a member of the body has an interest. EAO 220. See also, EAO 213; Attorney General Opinion JM-671 (1987), Attorney General Letter Opinion 93-12 (1993). See also Bexar County v. Wentworth, 378 S.W.2d 126, 128-29 (Tex. Civ. App.ΓÇôSan Antonio 1964, writ refΓÇÖd n.r.e.); Meyers v. Walker, 276 S.W. 305, 307 (Tex. Civ. App.ΓÇöEastland 1925, no writ); Attorney General Letter Opinion 93-12 (1993). ΓÇ£PERSONAL OR PRIVATE INTERESTΓÇ¥ DEFI- NITION. The term ΓÇ£personal or private interestΓÇ¥ does not include the interest of the board member in question to a bank, which is essentially that of an ordinary cus- tomer and consumer of products or services offered by the bank. EAO 218. See also Attorney General Opinion H-1319 (1978), Attorney General Opinion JM-671 (1987), Attorney General Letter Opinion 93-12 (1993). See also Bexar County v. Wentworth, 378 S.W.2d 126, 128-29 (Tex. Civ. App.ΓÇöSan Antonio 1964, writ refΓÇÖd n.r.e.); Meyers v. Walker, 276 S.W. 305, 307 (Tex. Civ. App.ΓÇöEastland 1925, no writ). MEMBERS OF TCSGA BOARD. The Texas Certified Self-Insurer Guaranty Association (TCSGA) board of directors is not part of the executive branch of state government. Although the TCSGA is statutorily cre- ated, its members are private employers who desire to become certified self-insurers for purposes of workersΓÇÖ compensation benefits for their employees. Labor Code ┬º 407.121. TCSGA receives no state appropriated funds. In light of these features of the TCSGA, we do not think the legislature intended that TCSGA be considered part of the executive branch of state government. Therefore, because TCSGA is not a state agency for purposes of chapter 572, the requirements of section 572.058(a) do not apply to state officers who are members of the TCSGA board when they are acting in their capacity as TCSGA board members. Because we have determined that the TCSGA is not a state agency for purposes of chapter 572, the revolving door prohibition is inapplica- ble to the self-insurer members of the TCSGA board. EAO 179. See also EAO 142.

sections.title: INDEPENDENCE OF STATE AND LOCAL OFFICERS ACTING IN
sections.content: LEGISLATIVE CAPACITY (a) 	In this section, ΓÇ£legislative measureΓÇ¥ includes: (1) 	a bill, resolution, order, or other proposal to adopt, enact, amend, or repeal a statute, ordinance, rule, or policy of general application; (2) 	a proposal to adopt, enact, amend, or repeal, or to grant a variance or other exception to, a zoning ordinance; or (3) 	a proposed constitutional amendment or charter amendment subject to a vote of the electorate. (b) 	For purposes of Subsection (a), a measure that is applicable to a class or subset of persons or matters that is defined in general terms without naming the particular persons or matters is a measure of general application. (c) 	To protect the independence of state and local officers acting in a legislative capacity, a state or local officer, whether elected or appointed, including a member of the governing body of a school district or other political subdivision of this state, may not be subject to disciplinary action or a sanction, penalty, disability, or liability for: (1) 	an action permitted by law that the officer takes in the officerΓÇÖs official capacity regarding a legis- lative measure; (2) 	proposing, endorsing, or expressing support for or opposition to a legislative measure or taking any action permitted by law to support or oppose a legislative measure; (3) 	the effect of a legislative measure or of a change in law proposed by a legislative measure on any person; or (4) 	a breach of duty, in connection with the memberΓÇÖs practice of or employment in a licensed or regulated profession or occupation, to disclose to any person information, or to obtain a waiver or consent from any person, regarding: (A) the officerΓÇÖs actions relating to a legislative measure; or (B) the substance, effects, or potential effects of a legislative measure.

sections.title: SOLICITATION OF OR RECOMMENDATIONS
sections.content: REGARDING CONTRIBUTIONS TO CHARITABLE ORGANIZATIONS AND GOVERNMENTAL ENTITIES (a) 	Unless otherwise prohibited by the Code of Judicial Conduct, a state officer or state employee may: (1) 	solicit from any person a contribution to: (A) an organization that: (i) 	is exempt from income taxation under Section 501(a), Internal Revenue Code of 1986, by being listed under Section 501(c)(3) of that code; (ii) 	does not attempt to influence legislation as a substantial part of the organizationΓÇÖs activ- ities; and (iii) 	has not elected under Section 501(h), Internal Revenue Code of 1986, to have that sub- section apply to the organization; or (B) a governmental entity; or (2) 	recommend to any person that the person make a contribution to an organization or entity described by Subdivision (1). (b) 	A monetary contribution solicited or recommended as provided by Subsection (a) must: (1) 	be paid or made directly to the charitable organization or governmental entity by the person making the contribution; (2) 	be in the form of a check, money order, or similar instrument payable to the charitable organiza- tion or governmental entity; or (3) 	be in the form of a deduction from a state employeeΓÇÖs salary or wage payment under the state employee charitable campaign under Subchapter I, Chapter 659. (c) 	A contribution solicited or recommended as provided by Subsection (a) that is not a monetary contri- bution must be delivered directly to the charitable organization or governmental entity by the person making the contribution. (d) 	A contribution paid as provided by Subsection (b) or delivered as provided by Subsection (c) is not: (1) 	a political contribution to, or political expenditure on behalf of, the state officer or state employee for purposes of Title 15, Election Code; (2) 	an expenditure for purposes of Chapter 305; or (3) 	a benefit to the state officer or state employee for purposes of Sections 36.08 and 36.09, Penal Code.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2005, 79 th Leg., Ch. 53 (H.B. 762), Sec. 1, eff. September 1, 2005.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: PROCUREMENT 	DEFINED 	FOR 	PURPOSES OF TITLE 15. The Government Code does not define procurement or contract negotiation. However, we have said a procurement involves an agencyΓÇÖs acquisition of goods and services including ΓÇ£defin[ing] the business need,ΓÇ¥ ΓÇ£select[ing] the vendor that provides best value to the State,ΓÇ¥ and ΓÇ£ensur[ing] that the awarded contract complies with applicable procurement law and contains provisions that achieve the procurement objectives.ΓÇ¥ Tex. Ethics CommΓÇÖn Op. No. 571 (2022), quoting the State of Texas Procurement and Contract Management Guide. Unlike the other Chapter 572 ΓÇ£revolving doorΓÇ¥ prohibitions [in 572.054], this provision applies to all former state employees and does not merely prohibit for- mer state agency employees from working on particular matters in their new employment. Compare id. ┬º 572.054, with id. ┬º 572.069. Instead, it prohibits former state agency employees from accepting any employment from certain persons for two years, even if the private employ- ment is unrelated to anything they worked on during their state service. Based on the test of 1. Whether the purchase of the vendorΓÇÖs products was a procurement, 2. Whether the requestor participated in the procurement, and 3. Whether the procurement involved the vendor in question, the former state employee would not be able to work for the particular employer for two years after the contract was signed. EAO 626. See also, EAO 586 (2023), EAO 571 (2022), EAO 568 (2021), EAO 545 (2017). STATE EMPLOYEE MAY NOT BE EMPLOYED IF HE PARTICIPATED IN CONTRACTS. Requestor is an employee of HHSC who plans on leaving to join a company with several state contracts. He expects to help manage payments to the state each month as well as helping with eligibility and quality control, but will not engage with the state contracts with HHSC. These are different particular matters than his work with the HHSC, so neither 572.054 would apply. This is the first opinion to address a state contract negotiation that was not also a procurement, but the same principle applies ΓÇô if the requestor gave approval, advice or recommendation on whether to enter into a contract at all, he participated and would be prohibited from employment with the company for 2 years. EAO 600. See also, Revolving Door #2: EAO 496 (2011), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997). Revolving Door #3: EAO 568 (2021), EAO 545 (2017). FORMER STATE EMPLOYEE MAY PROVIDE CONSULTING SERVICES. A former state employee became part-owner of a consulting business and that consulting business seeks to contract with one or more businesses that were involved in procurements that he participated in. Since the law specifies ΓÇ£employmentΓÇ¥ and the individual would be providing only consulting services through his own business, it is not prohibited by ┬º572.069. EAO 599. See also, EAO 582 (2022), EAO 572, EAO 545 (2017), Tex. AttΓÇÖy Gen. Op. No. GA-0292 at 4 (2005), Tex. AttΓÇÖy Gen. Op. No. DM- 409, at 5 (1996). INTERTWINING 	SBOE, 	TEA, 	PERMANENT SCHOOL 	FUND 	CORP 	REVOLVING 	DOOR QUESTION. The requestor is a former member of the State Board of Education ΓÇô all revolving door provisions will apply. Under 572.054(a): he must wait two years before appearing before or seeking to influence both the Commissioner of Education (officer of SBOE) and the PSF Corporation (because the Corporation board con- tains SBOE members). He would also be restricted with respect to TEA employees if they were also employees of the SBOE under the common law employee/er test. Under 572.054(b): since he participated in contracts that SBOE sent to PSF Corporation, he may not ever receive compensation under contracts that he participated in as an SBOE member. Under 572.069: he may not accept employment for two years from any person involved in any transactions which were subject to a ratification vote by the SBOE board during his tenure there. EAO 598. See also, Revolving Door #1: EAO 545 (2017), EAO 381 (1997). Revolving Door #2: EAO 496 (2011), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997). Revolving Door #3: EAO 586 (2023), EAO 571 (2022), EAO 568 (2021) CURRENT EMPLOYEE OF UNIVERSITY NOT SUBJECT TO REVOLVING DOOR, BUT MAY VIOLATE 	STANDARDS 	OF 	CONDUCT. 	The requestor has reduced his work hours at a university where he works to pursue outside consulting projects. The consulting firm specializes in executive searches for universities and he wants to submit a bid to provide con- sulting services to his university. Since he will maintain his employment, he is not a ΓÇ£formerΓÇ¥ employee and thus the revolving door provisions do not apply. But elements of 572.051, Government Code and the 39.06, Penal Code might apply re: standards of conduct, ethics policies, or use of nonpublic information to gain a benefit. EAO 595. RECEIVING COMPENSATION AS EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF NON-PROFIT. The laws under the Ethics CommissionΓÇÖs jurisdiction would not prohibit a legislator from solely receiving compensation from the organization, provided that the compensation reflects the actual value of the legislatorΓÇÖs services and not because of his status as a public servant; the services are provided in a capacity other than as a public servant and as long as the legislatorΓÇÖs official position is not a reason for his employment by the organization; the compensation is not received in exchange for an official act as a public servant; and the compensation is neither a prohibited political contribution nor a gift, loan, or other prohib- ited expenditure by a registered lobbyist. A legislator should understand that the solicitation of contributions to an organization for which the legislator serves as executive director and from which the legislator receives compensation for services could be viewed as improper under certain circumstances. EAO 508. See also Outside Employment by Public OfficialsΓÇöEAO 408, EAO 226, EAO 205, EAO 148, EAO 117, EAO 371, EAO 358, EAO 441, EAO 192; Solicitation of Contributions to OrganizationΓÇöEAO 427, EAO 150, EAO 97, EAO 19, EAO 178, EAO 123.

sections.title: CERTAIN EMPLOYMENT FOR FORMER STATE OFFICER OR
sections.content: EMPLOYEE RESTRICTED A former state officer or employee of a state agency who during the period of state service or employment participated on behalf of a state agency in a procurement or contract negotiation involving a person may not accept employment from that person before the second anniversary of the date the contract is signed or the procurement is terminated or withdrawn.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2015, 84 th Leg., R.S., Ch. 326 (S.B. 20), Sec. 4, eff. September 1, 2015.
metadata.ethicsOpinions: DIRECT COMMS RE: POTENTIAL CONTRACT WITH 	COMPANY 	& 	SUBCONTRACTOR TRIGGERS REVOLVING DOOR PROHIBITION. The requestor participated in the contract negotiation through his involvement in reviewing the contract, draft- ing contract terms, and giving advice and recommenda- tions to his supervisor regarding contract terms. Thus he is prohibited from employment with the company for 2 years after the contract with TXDOT was executed. A contract that identifies a subcontractor as performing work ΓÇ£involvesΓÇ¥ the identified subcontractor for purposes of Section 572.069 and also prohibits employment by the subcontractor for 2 years. EAO 586. See also EAO 578 (2022), EAO 568 (2021), EAO 545 (2017). AFFILIATES OF PROHIBITED PROSPECTIVE EMPLOYERS 	ARE 	DIFFERENT 	PERSONS NOT 	PROHIBITED 	FROM 	ACCEPTING EMPLOYMENT. Direct communications with a poten- tial contracting partner over the terms of a prospective deal constitutes participating in a procurement or con- tract negotiation. But, affiliates are different persons for purposes of Chapter 572 of the Government Code. Therefore, Section 572.069 of the Government Code does not prohibit a former employee of a state agency from accepting employment from an affiliate of a person that was involved in procurements or contract negotia- tions in which the employee participated during his state service. EAO 578 (2022). RECOMMENDING VENDORS DOES NOT = PARTICIPATION. An employee of a university system does not ΓÇ£participateΓÇ¥ in a procurement or contract negotiation by informally recommending a lawyer for outside legal services and would not be prohibited from accepting employment from the lawyerΓÇÖs law firm before the second anniversary of the date the employeeΓÇÖs outside counsel contract was signed. EAO 577 (2022). STATE AGENCY IS NOT A ΓÇ£PERSONΓÇ¥ FOR REVOLVING DOOR PURPOSES. All three revolving door provisions prohibit former state officers and employ- ees from representing, accepting employment, or receiv- ing compensation from certain ΓÇ£person[s].ΓÇ¥ As defined by Chapter 572, a state agency is not a ΓÇ£person,ΓÇ¥ so none of the revolving door provisions restrict former state officers and employees from accepting employment with another state agency. EAO 573 (2022). AFFILIATES/SUBSIDIARY 	COMPANIES 	ARE DIFFERENT 	ΓÇ£PERSONSΓÇ¥ 	FOR 	REVOLVING DOOR. Affiliates are different persons for purposes of Chapter 572 of the Government Code. Therefore, we conclude that section 572.069 of the Government Code does not prohibit a former employee of a regulatory agency from accepting employment from an affiliate of a person that was involved in procurements or contract negotiations in which the employee participated during her state service. EAO 572 (2022). MEDICAID 	APPLICATIONS NOT 	PROCURE- MENTS OR CONTRACT NEGOTIATIONS FOR REVOLVING 	DOOR 	ANALYSIS. 	This 	request raises several questions about the application of section 572.069. The first is whether the two locations of the same healthcare system are the same ΓÇ£person.ΓÇ¥ Information available from the healthcare systemΓÇÖs website and the Texas Secretary of State appears to confirm that the hospitals are not distinct legal entities, but merely two locations of the same organization. Therefore, it appears that the two hospitals are the same ΓÇ£personΓÇ¥ for purposes of section 572.069. Section 572.069 does not prohibit the requestor from accepting the employment because Medicaid applications are not procurements or contract negotiations. EAO 571. See also EAO 496 (2011), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997). FORMER STATE EMPLOYEE NOT PROHIBITED FROM ACCEPTING EMPLOYMENT. A former state employee who was a not a member of the procure- ment team, but as a member of agency leadership, was informed by the procurement team regarding project status may accept employment from a company that participated in a procurement. The employee did not ΓÇ£participateΓÇ¥ in the procurement as that term is defined in 572.054(h)(1). EAO 568. ΓÇ£RIGHT 	TO 	CONTROLΓÇ¥ 	TEST 	APPLIES 	IN DETERMINING 	EMPLOYER/EMPLOYEE RELATIONSHIP WITH CLIENT FOR PURPOSES OF 572.069. If a former state employee participated in a procurement or contract negotiation on behalf of the state agency with Potential Client, 572.069 prohibits the former employee from accepting employment from Potential Client until 2 years has passed since they left the agency employment. Whether or not the former state employee and Potential Client have an employer/ employee relationship depends on the following test, taken from Restatement (Third) of Employment Law ┬º1.01(a) (2015): (1) The individual acts, at least in part, to serve the inter- ests of the employer; (2) The employer consents to receive the individualΓÇÖs ser- vices; and (3) The employer controls the manner and means by which the individual renders services, or the employer otherwise effectively prevents the individual from rendering those services as an independent business- person EAO 545 (2018). See also, GA-0292 (2005) (applying common law test to determine meaning of ΓÇ£employed byΓÇ¥ in statute), DM-409, at 4-5 (1996) (DM-409) (applying common law test to define ΓÇ£employeeΓÇ¥ in indemnification statute). See Nationwide Mut. Ins. Co. v. Darden, 503 U.S. 318, 322 (1992). See also Kelley v. Southern Pacific Co., 419 U.S. 318, 323-24 (1974). FORMER 	TCEQ 	EMPLOYEE 	WORKING 	AS CONTRACTOR WITH PRIVATE FIRM. A for- mer TCEQ employee responsible for reviewing reports related to reimbursement of expenses for contractors did not prohibit the former employee from working as a con- tractor subsequently to work with the agency, with some limitations based on previous work. EAO 539. See also EAO 523 (2014), EAO 507 (2012), EAO 496 (2011), EAO 419 (1999), EAO 397 (1998), EAO 364 (1997), EAO 353 (1996), EAO 345 (1996), EAO 337 (1996), EAO 324 (1996).

sections.title: PROHIBITIONS AND REPORTING REQUIREMENTS RELATED TO
sections.content: FOREIGN INFLUENCE; CRIMINAL OFFENSE (a) 	In this section, ΓÇ£foreign adversaryΓÇ¥ means a country: identified by the United States Director of National Intelligence as a country that poses a risk to the national security of the United States in at least one of the three most recent Annual Threat Assessments of the U.S. Intelligence Community issued pursuant to Section 108B, National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. Section 3043b); or desig- nated by the governor after consultation with the public safety director of the Department of Public Safety. (b) 	An employee or volunteer of a state agency or a political subdivision of this state may not: (1) 	accept transportation to or lodging in a country that is a foreign adversary and that is paid for by the foreign adversary because of the employee ΓÇÖs or volunteer ΓÇÖs position with the state or political subdivision; or (2) 	accept a gift or item of value from a person representing a foreign adversary for any purpose, including to pay for travel expenses or as reimbursement for the costs of attending a conference or other event in a country that is a foreign adversary or that is hosted on behalf of a foreign adversary or a principal of a foreign adversary. (c) 	An employee or volunteer of a state agency or a political subdivision of this state shall report to the commission, in the form and manner the commission requires, each interaction, communication, or meeting the employee or volunteer has with a person acting on behalf of a foreign adversary not later than the 30th day after the date of the interaction, communication, or meeting. The commission shall make available a report under this subsection to the attorney general and the Texas Department of Public Safety on request. (d) 	A person commits an offense if the person knowingly violates this section. An offense under this subsection is a state jail felony.

title: FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE BY AND STANDARDS OF CONDUCT FOR

sections.title: APPLICABILITY OF CHAPTER
sections.content: This chapter applies only to a municipality with a population of 100,000 or more.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003.

sections.title: DEFINITIONS
sections.content: In this chapter: (1) 	ΓÇ£DeliverΓÇ¥ means transmitting by mail, personal delivery, or e-mail or any other means of electronic transfer. (2) 	ΓÇ£Municipal officerΓÇ¥ means the mayor, a member of the governing body, the municipal attorney, or the city manager of a municipality.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003; Acts 2015, 84th Leg., R.S., Ch. 223 (H.B. 1246), Sec. 1, eff. September 1, 2015.

sections.title: FINANCIAL STATEMENT REQUIRED
sections.content: (a) 	A municipal officer or a candidate for a municipal office filled by election shall file a financial state- ment as required by this chapter. (b) 	The statement must: (1) 	be filed with the clerk or secretary of the municipality in which the officer or candidate resides; and (2) 	comply with Sections 572.022 and 572.023, Government Code.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003.

sections.title: FILING DATES; TIMELINESS OF FILING
sections.content: (a) 	A municipal officer shall file the financial statement required by this chapter within the time pre- scribed by Section 572.026(a), Government Code. (b) 	A person who is appointed to a municipal office shall file the financial statement required by this chapter within the time prescribed by Section 572.026(c), Government Code. (c) 	A candidate for a municipal office filled by election shall file the financial statement required by this chapter not later than the earlier of: (1) 	the 20th day after the deadline for filing an application for a place on the ballot in the election; or (2) 	the fifth day before the date of the election. (d) 	Except as provided in Subsection (g), the timeliness of the filing is governed by Section 572.029, Government Code. (e) 	A municipal officer or a person who is appointed to a municipal office may request the clerk or secre- tary of the municipality to grant an extension of not more than 60 days for filing the statement. The clerk or secretary shall grant the request if it is received before the filing deadline or if the officerΓÇÖs physical or mental incapacity prevents the officer from filing the statement or requesting an extension before the filing deadline. The clerk or secretary may not grant more than one extension to a person in one year except for good cause shown. (f) 	The clerk or secretary may not grant an extension to a candidate for a municipal office filled by election. (g) 	A person is considered to have timely filed a financial statement under this chapter if: (1) 	the statement is personally delivered not later than 5 p.m. of the last day for filing the statement; or (2) 	the clerk or secretary of the municipality with whom the statement is required to be filed has adopted rules and procedures to provide for the electronic filing of the statement and the state- ment is electronically filed in accordance with those rules and procedures not later than midnight of the last day for filing the statement.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003; Acts 2013, 83rd Leg., R.S., Ch. 894 (H.B. 1035), Sec. 2, eff. September 1, 2013.

sections.title: FORM OF STATEMENT
sections.content: (a) 	The clerk or secretary of the municipality shall require that the form designed by the Texas Ethics Commission under Chapter 572, Government Code, be used for filing the financial statement. (b) 	The clerk or secretary shall deliver at least one copy of the form to each municipal officer or person who is appointed to a municipal office who is required to file under this chapter within the time prescribed by Section 572.030(c)(1), Government Code. The clerk or secretary shall deliver a copy of the form to each candidate for a municipal office filled by election who is required to file under this chapter not later than the 10th day before the deadline for filing the statement under Section 145.004(c). The clerk or secretary may choose one or more methods to deliver the form.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003; Acts 2015, 84th Leg., R.S., Ch. 223 (H.B. 1246), Sec. 2, eff. September 1, 2015.

sections.title: DUPLICATE OR SUPPLEMENTAL STATEMENTS
sections.content: If a person has filed a financial statement under one provision of this chapter covering the preceding cal- endar year, the person is not required to file a financial statement required under another provision of this chapter covering that same year if, before the deadline for filing the statement under the other provision, the person notifies the clerk or secretary of the municipality in writing that the person has already filed a financial statement under this chapter covering that year.

metadata.addedBy: Added by Acts 2003, 78th Leg., ch. 249, Sec. 6.01, eff. Sept. 1, 2003.

sections.title: PUBLIC ACCESS TO STATEMENTS
sections.content: (a) 	Financial statements filed under this chapter are public records. The clerk or secretary of the munici- pality shall maintain the statements in separate alphabetical files and in a manner that is accessible to the public during regular office hours. (b) 	Until the first anniversary of the date a financial statement is filed, each time a person, other than the clerk or secretary of the municipality or an employee of the clerk or secretary who is acting on official business, requests to see the financial statement, the clerk or secretary shall place in the file a statement of the personΓÇÖs name and address, whom the person represents, and the date of the request. metadata.ethicsOpinions: COMMUNICATIONS 	TO 	SOME 	COUNTY OFFICIALS NOT GOVERNED BY LOBBY LAW. Counties are administrative arms of the state. They are generally described, however, as ΓÇ£political subdivi- sions,ΓÇ¥ not as parts of one of the branches of ΓÇ£stateΓÇ¥ gov- ernment. Therefore, we conclude that communications to county officials are not governed by the lobby law. There are provisions, however, that impose reporting requirements on certain county officials in a county with a population of 500,000 or more. Local GovΓÇÖt Code ch. 159. Under those provisions, certain county officials must file a financial statement with the county auditor. Therefore, a county official in a county with a population of 500,000 or more may be required to report some food, lodging, transportation, or entertain- ment under that section in order to satisfy the require- ments of Penal Code section 36.10(b). sections.title: FILING DATES; TIMELINESS OF FILING
sections.content: (a) 	A county officer or justice of the peace shall file the financial statement required by this subchapter within the time prescribed by Section 572.026, Government Code. sections.content: If a person has filed a financial statement under one provision of this subchapter covering the preceding cal- endar year, the person is not required to file a financial statement required under another provision of this subchapter to cover that same year if, before the deadline for filing the statement under the other provision, the person notifies the county clerk in writing that the person has already filed a financial statement under this subchapter to cover that year.
